strategy.summary: Reproduce gh-23196/gh-24567 by building SciPy at the buggy commit 8b304446741a with the developer's test patch applied, then running the norminvgauss tail-accuracy tests. On the buggy revision norminvgauss(a=1,b=0).cdf(100) returns a value near 0 instead of near 1, and norminvgauss(a=0.1,b=0.09).cdf(1500) returns about 0.127 with an IntegrationWarning, so test_gh23196_tails_cdf_sf_accuracy fails. On the fixed revision (the PR's quadrature tail-switching) both assertions pass within rtol=1e-14. Success is the FAIL-to-PASS transition of that test, not any printed value.

pinned_because: numpy 2.0.2 is taken from the issue#25756 environment line only; no documented constraint or era ceiling exists, so this version is a chosen value and not a pin required by the defect
mpmath is unpinned; the test itself uses the R GeneralizedHyperbolic reference, not mpmath, so mpmath is not needed for the transition
cython, pybind11 and pythran versions are unbounded and not numerically relevant; the chosen versions are the ones present in the era builds, not requirements

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/stats/tests/test_distributions.py::TestNormInvGauss::test_gh23196_tails_cdf_sf_accuracy (parametrized over (x=100,a=1.0,b=0.0,ref=1.0) and (x=1500,a=0.1,b=0.09,ref=0.9999999999418577)); the companion test test_gh23196_tails_cdf_sf is also selected by the -k filter
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy commit 8b304446741a with the test patch applied, test_gh23196_tails_cdf_sf_accuracy fails (cdf(100) for a=1,b=0 and cdf(1500) for a=0.1,b=0.09 do not match the references at rtol=1e-14, and the 1500 case emits IntegrationWarning 'The algorithm does not converge'). On the PR head, the same selected tests pass, meaning all parametrizations of test_gh23196_tails_cdf_sf_accuracy and test_gh23196_tails_cdf_sf succeed.
strategy.numerical_probe: scipy.stats.norminvgauss(a=1,b=0).cdf(100) and scipy.stats.norminvgauss(a=0.1,b=0.09).cdf(1500), compared with 1.0 and 0.9999999999418577 respectively at rtol=1e-14
risks: The 1500 case depends on quad's extrapolation roundoff; the exact buggy and fixed values may vary across platforms, BLAS builds or SciPy versions, so the rtol=1e-14 transition may not hold identically on other machines.

The test's reference 0.9999999999418577 differs from the mpmath-based 0.9999999999364564 by about 5e-12, which exceeds rtol=1e-14; the test therefore relies on the R-derived value. If the fixed build lands between the two, the PASS side is fragile.

The developer test patch also adds subdir('test_generation') to scipy/stats/tests/meson.build and install_sources entries for reference_distributions.py and reference_distribution_infrastructure_tests.py. If those files are not present at the buggy commit, the meson build will fail before any test runs; ensure they are included in the test patch or the build will not transition.

The fix is pure Python in _continuous_distns.py, so the test does not need a special platform, but the wrong-value symptom was reported with a specific scipy-openblas build; no evidence shows that the BLAS backend affects the outcome, so this is an assumption.
Parametrized cases with a=10 and b_a near 0.9 are only checked at atol=1e-2 in the companion test; the accuracy test checks only a=1,b=0 and a=0.1,b=0.09.
The numpy version 2.0.2 and build tool versions are unbounded and were chosen, not documented; a different numpy 2.x may change integrator warning behaviour without changing the transition.

oracle.reference_source: R GeneralizedHyperbolic pnig(1500, alpha=0.1, beta=0.09) with options(digits=16), and the cdf(100) near-1 reference for a=1,b=0
oracle.why: The test compares against a high-precision external reference at a tight relative tolerance; quad roundoff in the deep tail is the only source of deviation.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision, norminvgauss(a=1,b=0).cdf(100) returns a value near 0 where the test expects 1.0, and norminvgauss(a=0.1,b=0.09).cdf(1500) returns about 0.127 where the test expects 0.9999999999418577; np.testing.assert_allclose with rtol=1e-14 raises AssertionError on the mismatch.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the PR head, the quadrature uses the mean-based tail switch and 1-SF / 1-CDF in the deep tails, so both cdf values fall within rtol=1e-14 of their references and the assertions pass.
